what: JD.com is a Chinese online retailer. Unlike marketplace rivals it buys and holds much of the inventory it sells and delivers it through its own logistics network, which is why its delivery is fast and its margins are thin.
customers: Chinese consumers, especially for electronics and home appliances, plus businesses using its logistics and procurement services.
money: first-party sales of electronics, appliances and general merchandise, plus marketplace fees
warehousing and delivery for itself and third parties
food delivery, overseas expansion and other ventures
moat: A nationwide warehouse and delivery network built over two decades, which lets it promise same-day or next-day delivery that marketplace-only rivals cannot match.
risks: Net margin of about 2% because it carries inventory and logistics costs
Chinese consumer spending has been weak
It has been spending heavily on food delivery, which loses money
Chinese regulatory and geopolitical risk affects all US-listed Chinese shares
opportunities: Cash of about $31 billion against $17 billion of debt
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
watch: Retail revenue growth and losses in the new businesses, especially food delivery.
